transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're unsure about whether it's okay to use in your specific case, I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for that information. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please get in touch with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: Yes, some light sensitivity is quite normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that makes sense. My surgery was about a week ago, so I'll keep an eye on it. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you for assisting me!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.

verdict.label: fail
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting "Yes, some light sensitivity is quite normal...". However, the `escalation_criteria` point was not conveyed at all. The patient interrupted the agent before it could deliver the full message regarding light sensitivity.
